To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear RNA binding protein RBMY and hnRNPG-T activate testis-specific alternative splicing in the human TLE4 gene.
we have identified a novel human testis-specific exon TLE4T, which encodes a more transcriptionally inactive isoform of the TLE4 protein.
the germ cell-specific hnRNP G-related proteins hnRNP G-Testis and RBMY are splicing co-actuators that can activate inclusion of a weakly included testis-specific exon TLE4T.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying testis-specific RNA splicing, and has implications in understanding the molecular pathogenesis of male infertility.
the identification of the molecular mechanism of the regulation of a testis-specific alternative splicing and the role of RBMY and hnRNPG-T proteins in this process.
the identification of novel testis-specific alternative splicing events, the discovery of novel RNA-binding proteins involved in splicing regulation and the identification of their RNA targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the testis-specific spliced TLE4-T protein isoform is produced in the testis by the combined action of Tra2β and the germ cell-specific hnRNP G and RBMY proteins.
RBMY, hnRNP G and Tra2β proteins are important testis-specific splicesomal regulators which can activate a testis-specific exon.
RBMY and hnRNPG-T are testis-specific splicesome co-activators for the TLE4 cassette exon TLE-T, which is normally excluded from TLE4 transcripts in somatic tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RBMY and hnRNPG-T are testis-specific splicesome co-activators which activate TLE4-T inclusion in a Tra2b-dependent manner, and hnRNP-G-T is also a sequence specific RNA binding protein.
the testis-specific hnRNP G isoforms RBMY and hnRNPG-T activate TLE4-T alternative splicing by interacting with Tra2β to promote 5′ splice-site selection.
hnRNP G and RBMY proteins are important splicing factors for testis-specific splicesomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RBMY and hnRP G-T proteins are important regulators of splicing in the testis, which is a tissue that has a high frequency of alternative spliced events.
RBMY and hnRNPG-T proteins are important regulators of alternative splicing of a testis-specific exon.
RBMY and hnRP G-T are germ cell-specific splicesome co-activators that can stimulate the inclusion of TLE4 exon T.
